item.title: North Bay police arrest two in connection with residential break and enter
item.description: The North Bay Police Service arrested two individuals in connection with a residential break and enter, in the 800 block of Worthington Street East. North Bay police responded to a report of a break and enter at a residence in the 800 block of Worthington Street East Feb. 20, around 8:20 a.m. Officers arrived quickly […]

item.title: Chris Sluman's many supporters continue to fight in his leukemia battle
item.description: Another weekend fundraiser added more than $75,000 dollars to North Bay Chris Sluman's cancer fight cause

item.title: Callander Museum considers future after last quintuplet passes away
item.description: Callander Bay Heritage Museum holding a meeting on new strategic plan on March 4 proposing more focus on logging, water, and rail history.

item.title: Propair officially takes flight in North Bay this week
item.description: Propair's route is from Rouyn-Noranda — North Bay — Toronto (Billy Bishop Airport)

item.title: Construction on North Bay apartment building restarts after 3 years
item.description: The project at 485 Second Avenue W. was put on ice during a legal battle with one of the financiers, which the developer won.

item.title: School bus company and drivers $1.10 per hour away from making a deal
item.description: Alouette Bus Lines offering raise to $20 per hour, but union demands a 'living wage' of $21.10, which is far less than other drivers make.

item.title: Fednor kicks in cash to try to encourage companies to look at defence sector opportunities
item.description: Government of Canada invests $472,859 to help Northern Ontario businesses diversify into the defence industry

item.title: Mark King and Chris Mayne turn up the heat over Cassellholme board removal
item.description: North Bay city councillors Mark King and Chris Mayne expressed frustration over their removal from the Cassellholme board and King wants the board investigated by the province
